verdict.headline: US-Iran mutual pause crashes oil as the year's most concentrated earnings week begins
verdict.label: Hold — 4 of 6 breached; Iran mutual pause removes oil-above-$100 FOMC input; Brent $89.73 / WTI $83.47 in premarket — clearance thresholds not yet achieved; FOMC July 29 + META/MSFT AH is the week's verdict
verdict.horizon: Through FOMC July 29 and Mag-7 earnings July 29-30
verdict.rationale_short: Monday morning premarket read-in: The weekend's defining development is the US-Iran mutual pause in hostilities — the US halted its 13-night airstrike campaign on Friday without formal announcement; Iran confirmed it would halt retaliatory strikes as long as the US pause holds; both sides held for a second consecutive day Sunday; and Oman-mediated talks on Hormuz transit have resumed. The pause is mutual but not a formal ceasefire: no written agreement, no Iranian concessions on Hezbollah or ballistic missiles, no Hormuz reopening timetable — both sides hold only conditionally. The direct market consequence: Brent crude crashed 7.3% to $89.73 from Friday's $96.78 close (and Sunday's $100.69 weekend high) — the largest single-session oil drop since the April 2026 ceasefire rally. WTI is down 6.5% to $83.47 from $89.31 Friday. This removes the primary FOMC-week risk identified in yesterday's morning brief: Warsh receiving a $100+ Brent input with institutional pressure to reintroduce tightening language in the July 29 statement. With Brent at $89.73, the inflation-expectation input entering the FOMC window is materially lower, though formal oil regime clearance requires Brent below $85 and WTI below $79 — the current $4.73 and $4.47 gaps remain live breach conditions. S&P 500 futures +1.02% (E-minis +75.75 pts, implied open ~7,487); Nasdaq 100 futures +1.68% (NQ E-minis +475.75 pts); VIX has declined to ~17.59 from 17.96 Friday; DXY pulled back to ~101.20 from 101.46; 10Y yield eased to 4.64% from 4.65%. Regime breach count: 4 of 6 breached — unchanged from Sunday but the directional vector has reversed for the first time in two weeks. WTI ($83.47, trigger_below $79) — $4.47 above clearance, still breached but first sub-$85 WTI print since the conflict escalated. Brent ($89.73, trigger_above $85) — $4.73 above clearance, still breached. 30Y yield (~5.09%, trigger_above 5.00%) — 2bps above trigger, still breached; bond markets partially pricing oil-relief but 30Y has not reclaimed the sub-5.00% level. September hike probability (82%, trigger_above 70%) has not repriced on FedWatch yet — the tool lags real-time oil moves by several hours — but a directional move toward 65-70% is the expectation as the Brent-sub-$90 input deflates the inflation-expectations component of hike pricing. SPX (7,411.98 Friday close, trigger_below 7,380) is intact with a 31.98-point buffer at Friday's close and gap-opening approximately 75 pts higher in premarket. BTC ($65,313 live at 11:01 UTC, Crypto.com, +1.24% 24h, range $64,410-$65,739) holds Gate 2 ($62,000) with a $3,313 buffer — extending the weekend session's conflict-phase stability into Monday's risk-on rally. The breach count is formally unchanged at 4 of 6 but the directionality matters: every prior session moved indicators deeper into breach; this morning is the first reversal of that trajectory. Kimi K3 open weights released July 26 at 7:30pm EDT — 2.8T params, ~50B active/token (MoE), 1M-context window, Modified MIT license, 1.4TB weight footprint, day-0 hosted access live on Together AI and Modal — the NVDA inference-pricing moat challenge is fully in the market as of this morning. The Iran-pause risk-on compression has offset the AI-sector overhang in premarket; NQ futures +1.68% despite Kimi K3. The week's event path: FOMC decision July 29 2pm ET (Warsh press conference 2:30pm; reduced-Brent input lowers tightening-bias language probability but does not eliminate September acknowledgment risk); META Q2 + MSFT Q4 FY26 Wednesday July 29 AH (EPS/rev clarity is the baseline; AI capex ROI guidance is the primary swing variable — GOOGL's -7% on $195-205B capex remains the investor template; MSFT FY27 CapEx est $262B is the headline risk); AAPL Q2 AH + AMZN Q2 AH + Q2 GDP advance estimate Thursday July 30. Durable Goods Orders this morning (est. +1.6% vs. prior -4.5%) is the opening data point. Do not chase the open gap — wait for confirmed gap-and-hold above 7,450 through the first hour before adding directional long exposure. XLE tactical trim: the Yanbu-Jizan add-back to 18-20% from Sunday's morning brief should be partially reversed — trim toward 15% at the open given Brent's $11 reversal from $100.69; the August CPI oil pass-through thesis is still partially intact at $89.73 but the near-term pressure is substantially reduced. Full XLE exit to 8% remains conditional on formal Iran-US ceasefire AND Hormuz transit confirmed above 10 vessels/day AND WTI two consecutive closes below $70.

trade_setups.thesis: Sunday morning's add-back to 18-20% was predicated on Brent holding above $100.69 and WTI at $92.19 into the FOMC window. The Iran mutual pause has reversed that — Brent at $89.73 removes the acute oil-shock FOMC-input risk and the XLE crude-shock premium should partially deflate. The August CPI pass-through thesis remains partially intact (Brent still above $85 trigger) so a full exit is premature, but holding 18-20% into a -7% Brent session on a verbal ceasefire is over-positioned against the current risk.
trade_setups.entry: Trim from 18-20% to 15% at Monday open. Maintain 15% as the Iran-pause base allocation. Conditions for rebuild above 18%: Iran resumes strikes AND Brent reclaims $95+. Conditions for full exit to 8%: formal Iran-US ceasefire agreed AND Hormuz transit above 10 vessels/day AND WTI two consecutive closes below $70.
trade_setups.invalidation: Iran formally resumes strikes before FOMC decision → Brent re-spikes above $95; rebuild to 20% immediately.
trade_setups.horizon: Through FOMC July 29; reassess with formal ceasefire/resumption binary

bear_case: The Iran pause is a verbal de-escalation with no formal agreement and reversible on a single strike by either side. Iran's preconditions (Hezbollah-Lebanon ceasefire, non-negotiable ballistic missile program) remain US red lines that Trump has not accepted; the pause is a tempo adjustment, not a resolution. The Yanbu export terminal remains a high-value target — two ballistic missiles successfully reached Yanbu Saturday and were intercepted by Patriot, demonstrating Iranian strike capability against Saudi crude infrastructure that is not removed by a 48-hour pause. A Yanbu strike resumption with confirmed terminal damage (Yanbu handles ~92% of Saudi seaborne crude exports after Hormuz closed) is the tail that reprices Brent above $105 overnight, drives the 30Y yield toward 5.25-5.35%, and forces Warsh to reintroduce tightening language at the July 29 statement — the identical path identified in Sunday's morning brief but now with a lower base probability. Brent at $89.73 and WTI at $83.47 are still above formal regime clearance thresholds ($85 and $79 respectively); 30Y yield at 5.09% is still above the 5.00% trigger; September hike probability at 82% has not yet repriced. The 4 of 6 breach count is formally unchanged. The FOMC meeting itself carries residual risk independent of oil: Warsh's July 29 statement with Brent at $89.73 (still 5% above the formal trigger and well above any pre-war baseline) may include explicit acknowledgment that September is live — different from the 'tightening-bias reintroduction' tail but sufficient to stall the relief rally and compress the SPX-7,380 buffer. The Mag-7 gauntlet is independently binary: if META operating margin compresses further from 41.4% and MSFT guides FY27 CapEx at $262B without credible AI monetization acceleration, the GOOGL -7% template is validated as a sector-wide AI capex multiple-compression rather than a company-specific event — a trade that has nothing to do with the Iran pause and is fully executable even as oil remains sub-$90. Bear case composite path: Iran resumes strikes before FOMC opens Tuesday → Brent spikes above $95 → Warsh July 29 statement acknowledges September explicitly → META and MSFT both show AI capex margin pressure → SPX closes below 7,380 by July 30 (formal BEARISH conversion) → Q2 GDP Thursday comes in below +2% (risk of negative revision) → target SPX 7,200-7,250 by July 31. Bear case invalidation requires all four simultaneously: formal Iran-US ceasefire signed (written agreement) AND Hormuz transit confirmed above 10 vessels/day AND FOMC explicitly closes September (probability below 55%) AND both META and MSFT demonstrate improving AI capex ROI with FCF improvement quarter-over-quarter. The probability of all four simultaneously within 96 hours is low — the Iran condition alone has not been met after 13 days of hostilities.
